questions.q: Why does `materialized='table'` stop scaling for a large fact table?
options: Table models are limited to 1,000 rows by dbt
Table models don't support ref() calls
It rebuilds the entire model from scratch every run, re-scanning full history for no benefit once only a small fraction of rows are new
Table models cannot be queried by BI tools
questions.explain: A table materialization drops and rebuilds from scratch every run — fine at small scale, wasteful once the source has years of history and only a few new rows per run.

questions.q: What does `is_incremental()` return on a model's very first run, and why?
options: False, because the target table doesn't exist yet, so the full select has to run to build it
True, because dbt assumes every run is incremental by default
It throws an error and the run fails
It returns the row count of the source table
questions.explain: On the first run there's no existing table to compare against, so is_incremental() is false and the whole SELECT runs to build the full table.

questions.q: What does `{{ this }}` refer to inside an incremental model's SQL?
options: The very first model in the dbt project's DAG
The model's own target table — used to find the current max watermark already built
The current dbt Cloud user running the job
A reference to the seeds/ folder
questions.explain: {{ this }} lets a model refer to its own target table from inside its own SQL — exactly what's needed to compare new source rows against what's already been built.

questions.q: Why is `unique_key` required for an incremental model but not a table model?
options: It determines which column gets indexed automatically
It has no real effect and is optional in every case
It sets the primary key constraint enforced by the warehouse
It tells dbt how to match an incoming row to an existing one, so re-running doesn't create duplicates instead of updates
questions.explain: Without a unique_key, an incremental model has no way to tell 'this is an update to a row I already have' from 'this is a new row,' so reruns can duplicate data.

questions.q: How does dbt's incremental materialization relate to the watermark pattern from the Snowflake course?
options: They are unrelated concepts that happen to share the word 'incremental'
The watermark pattern only works in Snowflake and has no dbt equivalent
It's the same idea, generalized — the target table itself acts as the watermark instead of a separate hand-maintained table
dbt's incremental materialization replaces MERGE entirely and never uses it
questions.explain: select max(...) from {{ this }} performs the same role as a hand-maintained load_watermarks table, except dbt reads and applies it automatically as part of the materialization.
